items.title: Clock time versus elapsed hours
items.pattern: 二時に / 二時間 + action
items.explanation: A clock point uses 時 and elementary time に. Duration adds 間 and normally precedes the action without the time-point に. 時間 also names time; interpret the whole phrase.

items.title: Years, weeks, months and dates
items.pattern: 今年 / 毎週 / 月曜日 / 四月 / 一日
items.explanation: Whole-word readings matter: 今年ことし, month 四月しがつ/九月くがつ, first date 一日ついたち versus whole-day duration いちにち. Use the complete taught tables and exceptions.

items.title: Compass position versus left/right
items.explanation: Compass directions stay fixed in the supplied map; left/right require an orientation. の links the reference point. Exit names use ぐち as whole words.

items.title: に for a standing position
items.explanation: The taught standing-position relation uses に, distinct from waiting activity at a place with で.

items.title: The person waited for
items.explanation: The awaited person is the object with を; waiting place uses で and a duration can appear without time-point に.

items.title: Invite a shared activity
items.pattern: いっしょに polite stem + ませんか
items.explanation: An explicitly shared-activity scene makes this an invitation, not an ordinary negative factual question. Use the taught stem.

items.title: Agree or propose: ましょう
items.explanation: Let's do the shared action. 待ちます → 待ちましょう; preserve the polite stem. It is not completed-action past.
